Summary: Jesus' persistence command in prayer: ask and it will be given, seek and you will find, knock and the door will be opened.
Commandment: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.
Application: Distinct from the Lord's Prayer pattern (live row), this is the manner of praying: persistent, childlike asking of a Father who gives good gifts, above all the Holy Spirit.
Purpose: Scripture's own reason: an earthly father gives bread, not a stone, to a child who asks — how much more the heavenly Father (Matthew 7:9-11).
Function: Prayer here is not a single request but a posture: ask, seek, knock — and keep at it. This comes from the New Testament, not from Sinai, so the old threefold division does not apply to it. Its goal was persistent, childlike asking of a Father who gives good gifts, above all the Holy Spirit. The evil it addressed was prayer that gives up too soon, as if God were unwilling or deaf. It restrained that evil with the picture Jesus gives: an earthly father gives bread, not a stone — how much more the heavenly Father.
